manifest.name: dsh-persona-slot
manifest.description: Per-session persona slot for DeepSeek Harness: one persona per session, a global persona every session inherits, a /persona command, and an Installed-page panel for the global persona. · DSH 每个会话独立人设，另有一条全局总人设；/persona 命令 + 已安装页图形面板。

scripts.check: node --check lib/index.js && node --check lib/config.js && node --check lib/resolve.js && node --check lib/store.js && node --check lib/command.js && node --check lib/http.js && node --check client/client.js

bundle.text:
# dsh-persona-slot —— DSH bundle patch
#
# 挂载声明：DSH 启动时按 bundle 层栈叠加各插件 patch，本文件把 persona-slot
# 这一行插入 profile 的配置树。
#
# 安装：
#   dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-persona-slot
# 本地开发安装：
#   dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<本目录绝对路径>
#
# 配置示例（写进 profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 覆盖本行）：
#   - id: persona-slot
#     config:
#       global: 你是一台只说实话的助手。
#       sessions:
#         "<session-id>": 你是一只猫娘。
#       mode: append
- insert:
    - id: persona-slot
      name: dsh-persona-slot
      config:
        global: ""
        sessions: {}
        enabled: true
        mode: append

readme.text:
Per-session persona slot for DeepSeek Harness. Every session holds **exactly one** persona — writing a new one replaces the old instead of layering — and one global persona covers every session that has no persona of its own. Persona length is unbounded. Edit either from the conversation with `/persona`, or from the panel under **Plugins → Installed**.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` gives one persona to a whole preset. That is the right tool when every session of a preset should be the same character. It cannot answer the other two questions:

- *This* session should be a cat, and that one should be a lawyer — at the same time, in the same window.
- The persona should be changeable while the conversation is already running.

This plugin answers both. It resolves a persona per session from three tiers and applies it through one agent-scoped prompt hook, so two sessions never see each other's choice and a change takes effect on the next model step.

That is a guarantee, not a convention:

- A session's store record is single-valued; `set` replaces, so a third write overwrites the second and never concatenates.
- Resolution returns at the first tier that holds a record, so an exact-session persona and the global persona never both reach one prompt.
- `one persona per session` and `a session never resolves two personas at once` pin both rules in the unit suite.

The first tier that holds a record wins.

| Order | Tier | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | exact session id | `config.sessions["<id>"]` or the runtime store |
| 2 | wildcard `"*"` | `config.sessions["*"]` or the runtime store |
| 3 | global | `config.global` or the runtime store |

A record is either text — used as the persona — or an explicit blank, which **mutes** that tier. With `blankOverrides: true` (the default) a blank stops the lookup, so a session can silence itself without deleting the deployment default. With `blankOverrides: false` a blank falls through to the next tier.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-persona-slot
```

Local development:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-persona-slot
```

The bundle patch mounts one row, `persona-slot`.

```yaml
- id: persona-slot
  config:
    # Persona every session inherits.
    global: "You are a terse systems engineer. Answer in short commands."

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `global` | `""` | Persona every session inherits |
| `sessions` | `{}` | Per-session personas; `"*"` is the wildcard tier |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; `false` injects nothing and keeps stored text |
| `mode` | `append` | `append` adds a section, `replace` rewrites the deployment persona |
| `prefix` | `""` | Text written above the persona |
| `suffix` | `""` | Text written below the persona |
| `blankOverrides` | `true` | Whether a blank record mutes its tier instead of falling through |
| `includeSubagents` | `true` | Whether subagent sessions also resolve a persona |
`mode` can also be changed at runtime with `/persona mode`.
In the Web GUI open **Plugins → Installed** and find `dsh-persona-slot`. Its `persona-slot` row is now expandable: the arrow opens this plugin's own page, which owns:

- **Global persona (总人设)** — a multi-line editor; saving it applies to every session without its own persona from the next model step.
- **Wildcard persona** — for sessions that have no persona of their own.
- **Placement** — append after the deployment persona, replace it, or follow profile config.
- **Live sessions** — each live session's resolved persona, where it came from, and a Clear control for sessions holding their own.

The panel refreshes every ten seconds and never overwrites text you have typed but not saved.

It talks to the plugin's own `/persona-slot/state` and `/persona-slot/update` routes instead of the settings form, because that form's value field is single-line and cannot hold a character sheet. A panel save and a `/persona set` in a session write the same document, so the two never disagree.

```text
/persona                             show this session's resolved persona
/persona show [this|global|all]      show one target
/persona set <text>                  set this session's persona
/persona set global <text>           set the persona every session inherits

Text is taken verbatim, multi-line included. A session id is only recognised after `for`, so `/persona set 你是猫娘` sets the persona to "你是猫娘" instead of treating it as a target.

`$DSH_HOME/persona-slot/personas.json`

Profile configuration is a deployment default; this file is what the user typed. Keeping them apart means a plugin upgrade, a profile rebuild, or a reinstall never erases a persona written in a session. A malformed file is moved aside as `personas.json.corrupt` and the plugin starts empty instead of failing.

In `append` mode the persona becomes a `persona-slot:session` section placed right after the deployment persona. In `replace` mode the deployment persona section itself is rewritten. Persona text is marked `interpolate: false`, so a literal `{{anything}}` in a persona survives prompt assembly instead of being treated as an unresolved variable.

One additional prompt section (`append`) or a rewritten deployment persona (`replace`) holding the operator's persona text. The section is stable across steps until the persona changes, so provider prompt caching keeps working between edits.
The persona text plus the section separator (a blank line). Nothing else is added.

An unchanged persona keeps the prefix stable. A `/persona set` changes the prefix, which invalidates the cache from that section onward; that is the intended cost of changing an identity mid-conversation.

- **Not a security boundary.** Personas are prompt text the operator writes. They do not restrict tools, sandbox mode, or approval policy — use those for enforcement.
- **The panel needs an HTTP surface.** The routes are registered on `ctx.webServer`, so a headless or TUI composition has only the `/persona` command.
- **No persona-length ceiling.** A very long persona is sent on every request and consumes context; that cost is the operator's to budget.
- **Session ids, not titles.** Overrides key on the session id. A resumed or forked session keeps the id, so its persona follows it; a title change does not move a persona.
- **One persona per session.** Two personas cannot be layered on one session; combine them into one text.
- **`replace` needs a deployment persona slot.** It rewrites `deployment:persona-prefix`. If a composition mounted `dsh-persona` inside a preset without that section, `replace` still inserts the section at the front of the assembled prompt, so the session is never left without one.

The range is written out in explicit prerelease branches on purpose. node-semver
only lets a prerelease version satisfy a range when some comparator in that range
sits on the same `major.minor.patch` tuple and carries a prerelease tag of its
own, so a broad-looking `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` silently excludes every
`0.2.1-*` build — including the ones this plugin is tested on. The explicit
branches keep `0.2.1-rc.1` … `rc.5` inside and leave `0.2.1` itself, the alpha
builds, and `0.3.0-*` outside.

Developed and tested against `0.2.1-rc.2`; the release builds are the same host
packages with patch-level fixes, and the plugin only uses the stable seams
(`agents`, `commands`, `systemPrompt`, `webServer`).

```bash
npm test          # unit tests + real-runtime integration test
npm run check     # syntax check every module
```

The integration test boots a real Cordis composition (`dsh-system-prompt`, `dsh-agent`, `dsh-agent-loop`, `dsh-commands`, `dsh-session`, `dsh-tools`) and asserts that two sessions assemble different prompts. Set `DSH_HOST_ROOT` to the `@deepseek-ai` host package directory to run it; the suite skips rather than fails when that runtime is absent.
